title: Run all of `test_dynamics.jl` on the GPU

body:
Resolves #6034 by adding support for `top_tke_flux` for any number of closures. For 1-5 closures we have manually unrolled methods. And for 6+ closures we have a recursive method. A test has been added that checks that the CATKE surface TKE flux is correct for 1-6 closures.

This fix should, in theory, also apply to `TKEDissipationVerticalDiffusivity`.
title: Fix the CATKE surface TKE flux for 4+ closures

body:
`extract_field_time_series` falls back to walking an object's fields with `getfield`. A type object's fields are cyclic (`DataType.super`, `TypeName.wrapper`), so reaching one overflows the stack. It is easy to reach: a closure that captures its float type stores the type as a field.

```julia
julia> using Oceananigans.OutputReaders: extract_field_time_series

julia> extract_field_time_series(let FT = Float32; (x, y, z, t) -> FT(1) / FT(2) end)
ERROR: StackOverflowError:
```

This adds `Type` to `CannotPossiblyContainFTS`.
title: Stop FieldTimeSeries extraction from recursing into type objects

body:
This requires more care than #5993, so I'm opening it is a separate PR on top of the other one.  This takes a much simpler and less invasive approach than #5614 (if desired, that refactoring can still be done, but not just for the sake of avoiding type piracy).  Let's see what CI says, but hopefully this won't break any test here.

Together with #5993 this removes all type piracies and fixes #5601.

> The `op(Lc, a, b)` and `op(Lop, a, b, c, d...)` methods generated by
> `@binary` and `@multiary` extended `Base` operators with signatures made
> only of foreign types: the location tuple is a `Tuple` whose element
> union includes `Nothing`, and the operand unions include `Number` and
> `Function`. A location-typed signature cannot fix the type-tuple sugar
> either, because `(Center, Center, Center)` is a `Tuple{DataType, …}`.
> Typing the operand instead makes every method non-pirate regardless of
> how locations are represented, and keeps the type-tuple sugar.
> 
> Binary operators now provide `(Lc, ::AbstractField, ::Union{Number,
> AbstractField})` and `(Lc, ::Number, ::AbstractField)`, sharing their body
> through `binary_operation`; the `Function` and `GridMetric` combinations
> already had their own methods. The `(Lc, ::Number, ::Number) = op(a, b)`
> method is removed. Multiary operators require their first operand to be
> an `AbstractField`, as the location-free sugar already did.
> 
> Field-free calls such as `+(Lc, 1, 2)`, `+(Lc, f, 2)`, `*(Lc, Δx, Δx)` or
> `*((Nothing, Nothing, Nothing), nothing, nothing)`, which used to return a
> number or a grid-less, unusable operation (see issue #5601), now fall
> through to `Base` and raise a `MethodError`. The explicit-location
> multiary form with a leading non-field operand, `+(Lop, 1, u, v)`, is no
> longer accepted either. Every call involving a field or a number next to
> a field is unchanged.
title: Resolve type piracy in AbstractOperations by requiring a field operand

body:
## Summary

`ReferenceToStretchedDiscretization` can hang forever instead of returning. The loop in
`compute_stretched_interfaces` grows the coordinate one interface at a time until it has covered
`extent`, but nothing guarantees that each iteration actually advances. When the new interface
rounds back onto the previous one, the coordinate stops growing and the loop spins indefinitely
at full CPU with no output.

This PR detects that case and throws an `ArgumentError` naming the likely cause.

## How it happens

There are two separate cases where the increment can go to zero:

1. **The stretching law shrinks the spacing.** `PowerLawStretching(power)` computes `Δ^power`.
   For `Δ > 1` and `power > 1` that grows, which is the case the defaults are tuned for
   (`PowerLawStretching(1.02)`, ocean-scale spacings in meters). For `Δ < 1` the same expression
   *shrinks*: `0.05^1.3 ≈ 0.02`. Each iteration then makes the next one smaller still, and the
   spacing tends to zero while the coordinate converges well short of `extent`.

2. **`rounding_digits` is too coarse for the spacing.** Interfaces are rounded with
   `round(…; digits = rounding_digits)`, default `2`. A spacing below `0.005` disappears entirely
   in that rounding, so `faces[end] + dir * Δ` rounds back to `faces[end]`.

Mechanism 1 feeds mechanism 2, so a soil- or snow-scale coordinate in Terrarium.jl usually meets both.

### Reproducer

    using Oceananigans

    # hangs on main
    ReferenceToStretchedDiscretization(extent = 100,
                                       constant_spacing = 0.05,
                                       constant_spacing_extent = 0.05,
                                       maximum_spacing = 20,
                                       stretching = PowerLawStretching(1.3))

## The change

`compute_stretched_interfaces` now compares each candidate interface against the previous one and
throws rather than pushing a duplicate:

    next_face = round(faces[end] + dir * Δ, digits=rounding_digits)

    if next_face == faces[end]
        throw(ArgumentError("cannot reach the requested extent $extent: …"))
    end

    push!(faces, next_face)

The message reports the extent, where the coordinate stalled, the spacing it started from and the
spacing it shrank to, and explains the potential causes: `PowerLawStretching` shrinks spacings
smaller than one whereas `LinearStretching` grows spacings of any size, and that `rounding_digits`
may be too coarse.

This is one comparison per interface, on a host-side constructor that runs once per grid, so there
is no performance consideration.

## Scope and compatibility

Non-breaking. Every set of arguments that previously returned a coordinate still returns the same
coordinate. The added check only fires on the path that previously did not terminate, and the condition
`next_face == faces[end]` is exactly the condition under which the loop cannot make progress.

## Tests

Two cases added to the `ReferenceToStretchedDiscretization` testset in `test/test_grids.jl`:

- the reproducer above now throws `ArgumentError` (previously: the test suite hangs);
- the same coordinate built with `LinearStretching(0.3)` and `rounding_digits = 6` succeeds,
  covers the requested extent, and has strictly increasing faces

## Context

Found while building soil coordinates (centimeter-scale spacing at the surface, stretching to meters at depth) for [Terrarium.jl](https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Terrarium.jl). The symptom there was an apparently frozen model constructor, which took a while to trace back to the grid.

## Alternative fixes

We could consider also simply blocking invalid configurations that would lead to this behavior rather than raising the `ArgumentError`. I'd be happy to change that if preferred by the core developers.
title: Fix buggy while loop in `ReferenceToStretchedDiscretization` constructor
